claims.text: The starting W–Cu composites exhibit voids and imperfect W–Cu interfacial contact.
A brief, high-pressure PEMF-assisted liquid-phase infiltration step can produce uniform Cu infiltration into a W scaffold.
PEMF-assisted infiltration enhances the wettability of molten Cu on W.
PEMF-assisted infiltration reduces void formation at W–Cu interfaces.
Electromagnetic forces generated by PEMF drive molten Cu into fine-scale features of the W network.
The proposed treatment promotes rapid wetting and consolidation without compromising the W structure.
Short processing times can limit grain coarsening.
Short processing times will prevent unwanted diffusion in the proposed W–Cu process.
Machine-learning optimization can identify pulse intensity and duration that minimize porosity and optimize W–Cu interfacial bonding.
The treatment can be conducted at 1100–1300 °C and pressures of several tens of MPa.
Temperatures of 1100–1300 °C are above the melting point of Cu and well below the melting point of W.
Reduced void volume and improved interfacial bonding will enhance thermal conductivity.
Reduced void volume and improved interfacial bonding will enhance mechanical durability under irradiation and cyclic thermal stress.
PEMF-assisted W–Cu composites will outperform vapor-coated and sintered W–Cu composites in void content, interfacial bonding, thermal conductivity, and mechanical durability.
Vapor-coated W powders can be sintered to achieve near-perfect W–Cu contact.
The vapor-coated and sintered W–Cu baseline still exhibits occasional defects and voids.
